examples.text: Я стою здесь.
examples.trans: I'm standing here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это я соврал, чтобы уйти пораньше.
examples.trans: I made that up so I could leave early.

examples.text: Да, это время нам отлично подходит.
examples.trans: Yes, that time suits us very well.

examples.text: Это мой очень близкий друг.
examples.trans: He is my very close friend.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Да, Лёва, что там случилось?
examples.trans: Yes, Lyova, what happened over there?

examples.text: Да, это время нам отлично подходит.
examples.trans: Yes, that time suits us very well.

examples.text: Вообще непонятно, чего от него ждать.
examples.trans: There is no telling what to expect from him.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Ладно, давай закажем себе по коктейлю.
examples.trans: Alright, let us order ourselves a cocktail each.

examples.text: Ладно, я тогда пойду, не буду мешать.
examples.trans: Alright, I will go then, I will not bother you.

examples.text: Да ладно, Костя, я совсем не против.
examples.trans: Come on, Kostya, I do not mind at all.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овсем').

examples.text: А вот Никита — совсем другое дело.
examples.trans: Now Nikita is a completely different matter.

examples.text: Привет, Лёва, я тебя совсем потеряла.
examples.trans: Hello, Lyova, I completely lost track of you.

examples.text: Он совсем не умеет мне врать.
examples.trans: He does not know how to lie to me at all.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'against', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Да ладно, Костя, я совсем не против.
examples.trans: Come on, Kostya, I do not mind at all.

examples.text: Я против.
examples.trans: I'm against it.

examples.text: Он против кластера.
examples.trans: He is against the cluster.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'until', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вы лучше спокойно дома отдохните.
examples.trans: You had better rest quietly at home.

examples.text: Ты обязательно пройдёшь полное обследование.
examples.trans: You will definitely undergo a full medical checkup.

examples.text: Нам ещё надо все плиты мыть.
examples.trans: We still need to wash all the stoves.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'end' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ты уже закончил работу, Лёва?
examples.trans: Have you finished work already, Lyova?

examples.text: Нет, конечно, мы вмешиваться не будем.
examples.trans: No, of course, we will not interfere.

examples.text: Работа закончилась, а вы всё ещё здесь?
examples.trans: Work is over, and you are still here?

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'пивать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to finish drinking'.

related.gloss: not to to finish drinking (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Этот коктейль до конца допивать нельзя!
examples.trans: You must not drink that cocktail all the way to the bottom!

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и допивать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to finish drinking on time.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'льзя').

examples.text: Я знаю, что вам нельзя работать.
examples.trans: I know that you must not work.

examples.text: Этот коктейль до конца допивать нельзя!
examples.trans: You must not drink that cocktail all the way to the bottom!

examples.text: Нельзя? Ладно.
examples.trans: Not allowed? All right.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'after all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ведь это же был ваш личный телефон!
examples.trans: After all, that was your personal phone!

examples.text: Угощайся, это подарок за счёт заведения.
examples.trans: Enjoy, it is a gift on the house.

examples.text: Ведь там на самом дне слишком крепко.
examples.trans: Because right at the very bottom it is way too strong.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Да, Лёва, что там случилось?
examples.trans: Yes, Lyova, what happened over there?

examples.text: У меня там было важное дело.
examples.trans: I had some important business over there.

examples.text: Да, Анечка, что там с анализами?
examples.trans: Yes, Anechka, what is up with the test results?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'амый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('the very').

examples.text: Он высокий и с красивыми усами.
examples.trans: He is tall and has a handsome mustache.

examples.text: Может, самое время Денису подойти к ней?
examples.trans: Maybe this is the right time for Denis to approach her?

examples.text: Пусть они лучше сами во всём разбираются.
examples.trans: Let them figure everything out by themselves.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'bottom, riverbed' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ведь там на самом дне слишком крепко.
examples.trans: Because right at the very bottom it is way too strong.

examples.text: Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: Too much to do.

examples.trans: It's too hard.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Ведь там на самом дне слишком крепко.
examples.trans: Because right at the very bottom it is way too strong.

examples.text: От этого крепкого коктейля я сразу усну.
examples.trans: From that strong cocktail I will pass out right away.

examples.text: Держи его крепче, Ваня!
examples.trans: Hold him tighter, Vanya!

meanings.en: to be liked, to make a good impression
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нравиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'pleased', paired with 'нравиться'.

examples.text: Синеозерск понравился в Москве больше других мест.
examples.trans: In Moscow they liked Sineozersk more than other places.

examples.text: Тебе понравился фильм?
examples.trans: Did you like the film?

examples.text: Не бойся, тебе понравится.
examples.trans: Don't be afraid, you'll like it.
